reviewedShaNote: Both blocking reviews record headSha 5803256fa. That commit is the PARENT of the first fix commit (git merge-base --is-ancestor 5803256fa HEAD exits 0; git diff --name-status 5803256fa..HEAD lists the production files). At 5803256fa the lane carried only the unauthenticated-peer settle, so all three of the issue's outcomes were genuinely absent and every FAIL grade in both reviews was correct FOR THAT TREE. This report records what the tree does now, and treats each finding as a real defect rather than a timing artifact.
reproducedWhat: All three required outcomes, each measured on real custodian processes, plus the two defects the reviews exposed in the evidence path itself: an oversized Unix socket path that killed the transport unattributably, and a repro whose own INCONCLUSIVE guard was tripped by the fix working.

requirementsEstablished.requirement: 1. A custodian whose broker or manager is gone exits on its own within a bounded time
requirementsEstablished.method: Launch a seat with a long-lived child, adopt it from a SEPARATE manager process, SIGKILL that manager without unwinding (the crashed-manager shape), then poll the custodian and report the seconds.
requirementsEstablished.afterCommand: COTAL_SEAT_UNATTENDED_MS=8000 COTAL_RUN=o1-head PROBE_BOUND_MS=60000 npx tsx .tmp/probe-orphan.mts   (production at HEAD)
requirementsEstablished.number: 7.92 seconds against an 8000 ms bound; unbounded (still resident at 45 s) before the fix
requirementsEstablished.shipped: UNATTENDED_MS = 10 minutes, overridable per launch by COTAL_SEAT_UNATTENDED_MS. The window restarts at each controller disconnect, so a manager that detaches and re-adopts keeps its seats (cell O2 holds a seat across 1.4x the bound through a re-adopt). The child is stopped with the custodian rather than orphaned, because the custodian owns the only reader of its PTY.

requirementsEstablished.requirement: 2. The suite runner waits for or kills the custodians it started before returning
requirementsEstablished.method: Run the REAL shard runner (bin/smoke/shard.mjs) over a suite list holding one suite that launches seats, emits a valid sentinel, and returns without reaping. Count survivors the way the ISSUE counts them: read /proc/<pid>/cwd, because the worktree path never appears in argv.
requirementsEstablished.number: 3 custodians launched, 0 orphans after, counted by /proc/<pid>/cwd
requirementsEstablished.shipped: bin/smoke/reap-seat-custodians.mjs. The shard names each run, sweeps after EVERY suite, kills only custodians carrying that run's marker, and fails the shard for a suite that passed but leaked one. It reports how many custodians it saw but could not attribute (79 on this host) rather than letting '0 reaped' imply a clean box, and it never touches another run's custodians, which would SIGKILL a live seat in a parallel lane.

requirementsEstablished.requirement: 3. A census is cheap: argv or an environment variable names the run
requirementsEstablished.method: Launch seats under a known run marker, then read it back from /proc/<pid>/cmdline and /proc/<pid>/environ, and time the census.
requirementsEstablished.number: 4 of 4 attributed by argv AND by environ; census 7.2 ms
requirementsEstablished.shipped: Every custodian carries `--cotal-run <marker>` on argv and COTAL_RUN in its environment. censusCustodians(run?) reads the argv half, which is world-readable, so a reaper never needs the owner's uid or a /proc/*/cwd walk. A custodian carrying no marker is never claimed: it cannot be attributed, and claiming it would be a guess.

acceptanceCommandGate.note: Both reviewers used `pnpm repro:1648` as the acceptance path and recorded BOTH sides VOID. That command now reaches a real verdict on both sides, run from the reviewers' own TMPDIR.
acceptanceCommandGate.revertedOutput: custodian settled within 30s of its child exiting: false / control: once the unauthenticated socket drops, it settles: true / DEFECT PRESENT (#1648)
acceptanceCommandGate.restoredOutput: custodian settled within 30s of its child exiting: true / control: once the unauthenticated socket drops, it settles: true / OK: an unauthenticated peer does not keep a custodian alive

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: Both production-revert gate sides were VOID: the run exited non-zero without reaching a named assertion.
reviewFindingsAnswered.status: WAS RIGHT, ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED
reviewFindingsAnswered.diagnosis: Not a missing assertion and not the import shape the brief guessed at. reviewer x's own note named the mechanism: 'The initial TMPDIR inside the worktree produced an overlong Unix socket path and prevented the scenario from starting.' A seat socket is <root>/<32 hex>/seat.sock, and sun_path holds 108 bytes including its NUL. Past that libuv does NOT fail: it copies into the fixed buffer, TRUNCATES, and listen SUCCEEDS on the shortened name. The custodian then chmods the path it meant to bind, throws ENOENT inside the listen callback where the enclosing promise cannot catch it, dies as an uncaught exception without writing its log, and the launcher reports only 'custodian exited before ready: pid N gone'.
reviewFindingsAnswered.reproOutputBefore: root length=73  implied socket path length=116 — FAILED: custodian exited before ready: pid 3482479 gone   (no custodian.log written)
reviewFindingsAnswered.truncationMeasured: 109 bytes -> creates seat.soc; 110 -> seat.so; 111 -> seat.s; 117 -> EADDRINUSE
reviewFindingsAnswered.reproOutputAfter: FAILED: seat socket path is 116 bytes, over the 107-byte limit for a Unix socket: <path>. The kernel would truncate it silently and the custodian would bind a different name than it cleans up. Use a shorter custody root (a deep TMPDIR inside a worktree is the usual cause).
reviewFindingsAnswered.fix: launchSeat refuses an oversized path up front (assertSocketPathFits). The custodian verifies it bound the path it asked for, and routes every listen-callback failure to reject so the log is written instead of dying uncaught. smoke-kit gains makeSeatRoot, which keeps a suite's custody root short enough and says on stderr when it falls back to /tmp. Every seat suite and repro:1648 now use it.
reviewFindingsAnswered.proof: The reviewers' TMPDIR yields a 121-byte socket (rootFits=false). pnpm smoke:seat-orphan and pnpm repro:1648 both run green from it now: exit 0.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: The restored repro printed INCONCLUSIVE ('the unauthenticated peer dropped before the child exited'), so it reached no named assertion even with the fix present.
reviewFindingsAnswered.status: WAS RIGHT, AND IT WAS THE TEST'S OWN BUG
reviewFindingsAnswered.diagnosis: The repro gates its verdict on the unauthenticated peer still holding the custodian when the settle window opens. That gate is correct in intent, but it was read as 'did this socket close'. A settling custodian tears down its listener and closes that socket itself, so once the defect is FIXED the close is caused by the very behaviour under test. The script therefore reported INCONCLUSIVE on a tree where the custodian settled correctly, and both reviews recorded that as the fix being unproven.
reviewFindingsAnswered.fix: The discriminator is now the CHILD'S state at the moment the socket closed, captured in the close handler rather than sampled by a poll. Child still running means the peer left on its own and the scenario never armed; child already gone means the settle closed it.
reviewFindingsAnswered.proof: Reverted side exit 2 (DEFECT PRESENT), restored side exit 0 (OK), both from the reviewers' TMPDIR.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: Requirement 1 FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE: no manager monitoring, no bounded liveness timeout; the custodian only settles once the child has exited.
reviewFindingsAnswered.commandThatDemonstrates: COTAL_RUN=o1-base PROBE_BOUND_MS=45000 npx tsx .tmp/probe-orphan.mts with production at 43a4281a4 -> ORPHAN, exit 2; at HEAD -> EXITED after 7.92 s, exit 0.
reviewFindingsAnswered.note: reviewer g's reading of the base code was exact: settleTerminal returns early while `alive` is true, so a live child plus a dead manager was an unbounded wait. That is the defect the unattended timer closes.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: Requirement 2 FAIL: no suite runner was modified to track, await or reap spawned custodians; shard.mjs reaps smoke brokers only.
reviewFindingsAnswered.commandThatDemonstrates: PROBE_LEAK=3 node .tmp/probe-runner.mjs -> 3 launched, 0 orphans after (by /proc/<pid>/cwd), runner_reported_leak true, runner_failed_the_shard_for_it true; exit 0.
reviewFindingsAnswered.reviewerXCaveatAnswered: reviewer x noted that zero post-run orphans proves nothing when the tests clean up after themselves. Correct, and that is why the probe's suite deliberately does NOT clean up: it launches seats, prints a valid sentinel, exits 0, and the runner is the only thing that could have reaped them.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: Requirement 3 FAIL: the launcher spawns with only PATH in its environment and no identifying argv.
reviewFindingsAnswered.commandThatDemonstrates: COTAL_RUN=o3-final PROBE_SEATS=4 npx tsx .tmp/probe-census.mts -> 4 of 4 attributed by argv and by environ, census 7.2 ms; exit 0.
reviewFindingsAnswered.reviewerXCaveatAnswered: reviewer x excluded its own live sample because the matching shell contained the custodian path in its script text, so the sample matched the enclosing shell. censusCustodians avoids that class of error by requiring BOTH an argv entry ending in /dist/custodian.js AND the --cotal-run flag; a cell asserts a census for a different run claims none of this run's custodians.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: implementations/manager/smoke/seat-input-live.smoke.ts continues to leak orphaned custodians (PPID 1) on exit.
reviewFindingsAnswered.status: RIGHT, AND IT EXPOSED A SECOND REAL GAP
reviewFindingsAnswered.staticEvidence: mgr.stop() is the last statement of the try block, OUTSIDE the finally; the finally kills only the broker and removes the temp dir. A manager stop releases (detaches) its seats rather than reaping them, so a failure before that line leaves live custodians. I did not RUN this suite: its file is *-live and it needs a live broker, and the brief forbids a :live suite.
reviewFindingsAnswered.gapFound: Those suites build a child environment by copying their own and deleting every COTAL_ key, which is the right rule for connection material and takes COTAL_RUN with it. The marker degraded to the launching pid, so the runner's census could not attribute exactly the custodians most likely to leak.
reviewFindingsAnswered.reproCommand: npx tsx .tmp/probe-scrub.mts   (spawns a child through the real COTAL_ scrub)
reviewFindingsAnswered.fix: runMarker climbs the process ancestry and reads COTAL_RUN from the nearest ancestor that still carries it, bounded to 16 hops, stopping at pid 1. The scrub is unchanged and no suite has to remember an exception. Because the custodian's own exit is now bounded, such a leak is also self-limiting even when no reaper runs.
reviewFindingsAnswered.testingNote: /proc/<pid>/environ is fixed at EXEC and is never updated by a later assignment to process.env, so a test that sets process.env at runtime proves nothing. The cells use a parent actually exec'd with COTAL_RUN, and an armed cell asserts the scrub really removed it first.

reviewFindingsAnswered.finding: Self-found, not from a review: the orphan.smoke.ts scrub-chain cell spread the ambient environment into a child.
reviewFindingsAnswered.detail: The gate refuses `{ ...process.env }` into a child because whatever runs a suite may itself be a managed agent session carrying a live creds path and control token. My new cell did exactly that and the gate failed the suite for it (exit 1, naming orphan.smoke.ts line 392).
reviewFindingsAnswered.fix: The cell passes PATH and COTAL_RUN only. That is also a stronger fixture: the marker cannot arrive by some other inherited route.
reviewFindingsAnswered.proof: pnpm smoke:suite-ambient-env exit 0; pnpm smoke:seat-orphan still 32 cells exit 0 with the scrub cells armed.

productionChange: A custodian with no authenticated controller now stops its child and exits after UNATTENDED_MS, armed whenever the controller set empties and disarmed the moment one authenticates. Every custodian carries --cotal-run <marker> on argv and COTAL_RUN in its environment, recovered from an ancestor when a suite has scrubbed COTAL_; censusCustodians reads it back from /proc/<pid>/cmdline. launchSeat refuses a socket path the kernel would truncate, and the custodian verifies the path it bound and logs any startup failure instead of dying uncaught.
testAdded: packages/seat/smoke/orphan.smoke.ts — 32 cells, gated into smoke:ci via bin/smoke/ci-suites.d/. Covers the three required outcomes on real processes, the re-adopt case that must NOT trip the bound, the socket-path ceiling, and the COTAL_ scrub recovery.
